title: Pressurised pipe flow
process: steady full-pipe flow under a held tailwater, forward and reversed
equations: Manning full-pipe friction: h_f = L (Q n / (A R^(2/3)))^2, A = pi D^2 / 4, R = D / 4 (SWMM's law for gravity conduits, full or not)
Darcy-Weisbach: h_f = f (L/D) V^2 / (2g), f by Colebrook-White (Swamee-Jain alongside)
initialConditions: the junction at the tailwater level (so the pipe starts full); inflow ramped 0 to Q over 600 s
boundaryConditions: inflow Q at the junction; FIXED outfall stage 0.5 m above the inlet crown (the pipe falls 0.4 m, so it is full end to end). Reversed: the outfall (pool) at the high end, the inflow at the low end: flow uphill against the drawn direction.
geometry: one circular conduit, L 200 m, slope 0.002; no entrance or exit loss written
solver: SWMM 5.2.4 dynamic wave, EXTRAN surcharge, fixed 1 s step

reference.sources: Manning (1891); Colebrook (1939); Swamee and Jain (1976); Henderson, Open Channel Flow (1966) 4.4 for Strickler
reference.crossCheck: refs.test.mjs: Colebrook against Swamee-Jain (1.5 %, Re >= 1e5) and Colebrook's residual

outputs: head loss against Darcy-Weisbach (physical-model, not independently validated)
criteriaNotes: Manning head loss within max(5 mm, 1 %). The Darcy-Weisbach row has no criterion: it shows the model-form difference of Manning's law, under an assumed roughness equivalence, and is Not independently validated. Steady: head range over the last 600 s within 1 mm, else Numerically unstable. A pipe not full at every sample is an Invalid setup.
conservation: flow through the conduit equals the inflow (0.1 %); SWMM's continuity error reported
assumptions: steady full flow: no inertia; the velocity heads at the two ends cancel (one section)
limitations: SWMM applies Darcy-Weisbach only to force mains; a gravity conduit uses Manning when full, so the Darcy-Weisbach row is model-form, not a test of SWMM's implementation
validRange: circular pipes full end to end, steady, Re 3e5 to 3e6

criteriaRevisions.why: first registration, before the first run
